answer: A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 141 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The horizon detector writes to mirror, and oasis shows every merge. Submissions that land within 256 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
